# ChordPic

> ChordPic (https://chordpic.com) is a free, browser-based guitar chord diagram creator. Click on a fretboard to place fingers, see the diagram update live, then download it as SVG or PNG or share it as a link. No account or install needed. A paid Pro plan removes the watermark and ads and adds a hand-drawn style.

Key facts:

- What it makes: chord diagrams (a.k.a. chord charts, chord boxes, fretboard diagrams) for guitar and other fretted instruments; also works for scale diagrams.
- Customisable: number of strings, tuning of each string, starting fret, number of frets, title and title font size, optional fret markers.
- Editor: click to add/remove fingers; drag or swipe across strings for barres; click the O/X markers above strings to cycle open / silent / hidden; per-finger, per-barre and per-marker text labels, colors and shapes; string labels.
- Export: SVG, or PNG in four sizes (small, medium, large, huge). PNG width is fixed; height depends on the diagram.
- Sharing: "Generate Sharing Link" encodes the whole diagram in the URL. The link opens with the chord loaded and shows a preview image in chats and social posts.
- Pricing: Free ($0) includes all editing features, with a watermark and ads. Pro costs $4/month or $30/year and removes the watermark and ads and unlocks a hand-drawn diagram style.
- Languages: English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Russian, Portuguese, Italian, Urdu, German, Persian, Dutch, Indonesian, Korean (at /{lang}, e.g. /de, /es).
- Typical users: guitar teachers, lesson worksheets, songbooks and books, blogs and websites, YouTube thumbnails and videos.
